quote.quote: The committee was asked to vote on whether the overall benefit-risk assessment is favorable for the use of SUL-DUR for treatment of patients with HABP/VABP caused by susceptible strains of ABC organisms. There were 12 "yes" votes, 0 "no" votes, and 0 abstentions.

concern_quote.quote: The committee agreed that the study demonstrated compelling results for the efficacy of sulbactam-durlobactam in reducing mortality in HABP/VABP caused by ABC but highlighted the limitations of a small safety database and recommended that augmented postmarketing surveillance be conducted to collect more safety data.

change_quote.quote: Consequently, a postmarketing requirement to conduct a single-arm, open-label, prospective trial of the safety of sulbactam-durlobactam in patients with *Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus* complex infections will be requested upon approval.

summary: The Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee met on April 17, 2023, and voted 12-0 (0 abstentions) that the overall benefit-risk assessment for sulbactam-durlobactam (XACDURO) was favorable for HABP/VABP caused by susceptible Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus complex strains. While endorsing the efficacy data, the committee flagged the limited safety database and recommended augmented postmarketing safety surveillance. In response, FDA planned a postmarketing requirement for a single-arm, open-label prospective safety trial upon approval; a REMS was not required.
